final:
STATUS: pass

SUMMARY: I found no reproduced correctness or security failure in the ETag middleware, README row, or wrapper forwarding. Two wire-level deviations from the literal criteria (101 handling, Last-Modified removal) and one edge (handler-set empty ETag gets overwritten) are reproduced but minor. Probe files were deleted; `git status` is unchanged (README.md modified, etag.go and etag_test.go added).

FILES TOUCHED: none (probe files zz_probe*_etag_test.go were created and removed)

FINDINGS:
- [minor] 101 Switching Protocols is treated as informational: `WriteHeader(101)` then `Write("x")` over a real server gives status 101 and the server logs `http: superfluous response.WriteHeader call from ...startStreaming (etag.go:92)`. Bare net/http returns `ErrBodyNotAllowed` from Write and logs nothing. Criterion 6 covers 1xx generally, so this is a judgment call. Reproduced.
- [minor] Last-Modified is deleted on 304. Criterion 4 says the 304 "keeps … other headers" and lists only Cache-Control, Vary, Date, Expires and Content-Location. The code's comment says it mirrors net/http's writeNotModified, which also drops Last-Modified when an ETag is present. Reproduced: a 304 for `If-None-Match: *` came back with Last-Modified="". Needs an orchestrator decision.
- [minor] A handler that sets `ETag` to an empty string gets a computed tag written over it (`Header().Set("ETag","")` → tag returned). Reproduced. Criterion 3 says handler ETags are never overwritten, but an empty value arguably isn't one.
- [minor] `*,` and `"a", *` give 200 while net/http gives 304. This is the accepted "`*` only as whole value" deviation, so it is not a finding; recorded for completeness.

CHECKS:
- HEAD over real server (chi router, GetHead-style Handle) → 200 with ETag and Content-Length 5; with matching If-None-Match → 304, no Content-Length, no Content-Type. pass
- GET with `W/` request tag over real server → 304, empty body. pass
- Flush over real server: first chunk reaches client before handler resumes; later write streams; no ETag. pass
- NewResponseController.Flush / SetWriteDeadline / Hijack via Unwrap on real server (including Hijack after Flush). pass
- Hijack on recorder without support → "chi/middleware: http.Hijacker is unavailable on the writer". pass
- If-None-Match parity against http.ServeContent with the same ETag, about 45 inputs (weak/strong, `"x"` vs `"xy"`/`"X"`, empty, whitespace, unquoted, unterminated, `W/abc`, `,,`, empty members, malformed-stops, lists with whitespace, `""`, `W/""`, obs-text bytes, multi-line with malformed first line). Only the `*` mid-list cases differed (accepted deviation). pass otherwise
- 103 then 200 over real server → final 200, ETag of body. pass
- HEAD + Flush → 200, no ETag. pass
- Handler panic propagates (not swallowed). pass
- Handler-declared trailer set after Write, over chunked real server → trailer delivered. pass
- Compress and ETag in both orders with gzip Accept-Encoding; If-None-Match with the tag → 304, no Content-Encoding. pass
- `go test -race ./middleware -run TestETag` → ok after cleanup. pass

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should the 304 keep Last-Modified (literal criterion) or drop it (net/http)? Should 101 count as informational under criterion 6? Should an empty handler-set ETag be treated as "set"?
